mika_sales: Heads-up — Large enterprise just verbal on a 3yr commit. Their app mixes chat (few-shot prompts) + batch embeddings. They want: predictable 99th percentile latency, 2x daily business-hour surge, and a hard cost target. Can eng help size reserved GPUs vs burst credits?
noah_eng: Congrats! Can you post a short traffic profile? qps by hour, percent embeddings, avg tokens per request, and tail-latency SLOs.
mika_sales: Sure — quick numbers from presales test: peak concurrent RPS: ~650 rps (10:00–11:30), steady-state 80 rps nights. Mix: 65% chat (median 180 tokens, 95p 1200 tokens), 35% embeddings (avg doc batch ~16 texts). SLO: 95p < 1200ms, 99p < 2000ms.
anya_ml: With that 95/99 tail and long 95p token lengths, quantized Llama variants help but KV cache and CPU pinning matter for chat. Embeddings are cheaper per token but batchable.
sarah_sre: For predictable latency we should prefer reserved pools for the hot path. Autoscale with reserved baseline + burst pool to handle the 2x surge. We can cap cold-starts with a prewarm schedule.
kai_ops: Practical ask: do they want single-region hard SLA? If yes, reserve capacity per-AZ. Also need to know tolerance for degraded models (quantized fallback) during evictions.
leah_security: Security Q: They require KMS integration + customer VPC for logs. That pushes this to Dedicated or Private; hosted bursts still possible but must ensure no egress of PHI. Need their SOC2/PCI answers to sign off.
finance_ops: Pricing constraint — they want a blended per-token target ~40% below our list for that throughput. We can model reserved baseline to hit their target; burst credits priced separately. Will need committed minimum.
noah_eng: Sizing approach suggestion: simulate request mix through our perf profiles. Quick back-of-envelope: to hit 650 rps peak with 99p under 2s, we'd likely need ~6-8 A100-like reserved devices (depending on model variant), with 2–3 extra as burst pool or prewarmed instances. If they accept int8 quantization we can drop reserved to ~4–5.
anya_ml: Also recommend separate embedding workers optimized for batch throughput (lower latency SLO), they can run on cheaper T4-like instances. Splitting chat vs embed routes reduces interference and lowers cost.
mika_sales: They asked about autoscale policy — prefer automatic up to X with canary fallback to smaller model if tailing. Any suggested policy config?
sarah_sre: Recommended policy: baseline reserved capacity covering 70–75% of expected peak, scale-out threshold at 65% CPU/GPU utilization with cooldown 90s, max burst to +50% for 15min windows. Add model-fallback policy: if queue > 200ms for >30s, route to quantized variant.
kai_ops: We'll also propose preheat windows (start 15m before expected surge) for KV warm and avoid cold starts. Add a scheduled warmup daily at 09:45 for their traffic pattern.
leah_security: Note for Private: we must run an audit for KMS access patterns and bring-your-own-key. That adds ~2 weeks to private onboarding. Ping me their questionnaire now.
finance_ops: I'll draft a draft commercial: reserved monthly commit for baseline + burst credits bucket with per-minute metering. Include cost delta for int8 vs fp16 and for separating embedding runners.
noah_eng: Action items: 1) I will run perf sim with their 650rps mixed profile (need sample payloads). 2) Anya will estimate model variants cost/latency tradeoffs. 3) Kai/Sarah will author autoscale + preheat runbook. 4) Leah to review sec questionnaire.
mika_sales: I'll share payload samples and client security questionnaire today. ETA for perf sim?
noah_eng: Give me 48 hours after samples. Will attach a short spreadsheet with capacity vs cost options.
deploy-bot: Scheduled run: load-sim job started (job-id: ls-2026-5250). Logs: https://internal.redwood/load-sim/ls-2026-5250
anya_ml: One more note — eval set for quality regression is critical if we use lower-precision fallbacks. We'll lock a prompt set and install regression alerts in Optimize.
mika_sales: Great — thanks team. I'll coordinate a 30m sync with customer and invite engineering for the perf review.
noah_eng: Perfect. If customer commits to cross-region fallback later, we can shave reserved by ~10% using cross-region overflow. We'll include that optional config.
leah_security: Put security answers in the thread and mark any PII flow rules.
mika_sales: Will do. Closing loop after perf sim posts results. :thumbsup:
